decision_context: New high-conviction short initiation after market close.
human_initiation_rationale: The short was initiated because Zoom's reported Q1 strength and high valuation looked backward-looking, while FY22 guidance implied roughly flat sequential revenue, Microsoft Teams had reached huge bundled scale, reopening threatened pandemic-pulled-forward demand, and the Five9 deal looked like a large, all-stock, integration-heavy move to buy adjacent growth.
selected_inputs: Zoom Q1 FY22 financial results and guidance
Zoom/Five9 acquisition announcement and merger mechanics
Short-interest and borrow/crowdedness notes from the research file

known_catalysts.event_or_condition: Upcoming Zoom Q2 FY22 earnings report
known_catalysts.why_it_mattered: The next earnings print and Q3 guide could expose whether the guidance-implied sequential revenue plateau was real.

known_catalysts.event_or_condition: Market digestion of the Five9 transaction
known_catalysts.why_it_mattered: Investors could reframe the deal from offensive TAM expansion to defensive, dilutive, integration-heavy revenue acquisition.

known_catalysts.event_or_condition: Post-Labor Day return-to-office and hybrid-work normalization
known_catalysts.why_it_mattered: Reopening could reduce low-end/prosumer urgency and increase subscription rationalization, especially for customers not deeply embedded in enterprise workflows.

evidence_for_short: FY22 guide implied about $1.01B per quarter for Q2-Q4 after a $956.2M Q1, much slower than the 191% YoY headline.
The stock still traded at roughly 26x guided FY22 revenue after adjusting for cash, despite the implied sequential slowdown.
Microsoft Teams reached about 250M monthly active users, strengthening the bundled-competition argument.
The Five9 deal introduced a $14.7B all-stock transaction, delayed close, approval risk, integration risk, and a potential signal that core video growth needed adjacent M&A support.
ZM was below the 200D, 40W, and 10M averages and about 37.5% below its 2020 high while broad technology benchmarks were strong.
Short interest appeared low, reducing crowded-short and mechanical squeeze risk.
evidence_against_short: Zoom was highly profitable and generated $454.2M of Q1 free cash flow.
Zoom had $4.7B of cash and marketable securities.
Customers with more than 10 employees, large customers, and NRR metrics were still strong.
Hybrid work could prove durable and extend paid usage.
Zoom Phone, Zoom Rooms, Zoom Events, and Five9 could broaden the platform beyond core Meetings.
Delta-variant uncertainty could delay reopening and preserve remote-work demand.
The stock was not technically broken across every timeframe because it was still above the 100D, 150D, and 20M moving averages.
Upcoming earnings created gap risk for a common-equity short.
price_confirmation_notes: Price action supported the short as relative weakness and failed pandemic-leader recovery, but not as a completed downtrend. The setup required risk-controlled sizing and explicit invalidation.
